apworld-v0.2.1.description:
# so2.apworld 0.2.1

Version 0.2.1 of the Archipelago world for *Star Ocean: The Second Story* adds the **bench**: in
open world with character items and in hub mode, every member you haven't excluded can join, up
to 12, and you choose who fights. It also fixes open-world games that couldn't be generated with
`expel_progression` or `expel_teleporter` off, lets Skillsanity's skill guild checks and learn
levels hold progression items, and adds the **hell seed**: no random battles, with all the
training done in a free Fun City arena. It plays on **Shattered Stars 0.02.51** and later
(0.02.50 plays the seeds without the bench).

The world now has releases of its own, apart from [the game's](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/v0.02.51), so either can be updated
without the other. Get the game from
[Shattered Stars 0.02.51](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/v0.02.51).

## What's new: the bench

In 0.2.0 the party had the game's 8 places. In open world with `character_items`, and in hub
mode, the item pool held only as many members as fit with the hero: a random choice when you
allowed more, and the others never joined. Now there is a **bench** of 4 more places, kept by
Shattered Stars 0.02.51:

- **Every member you haven't excluded is in the pool**, with no random choice: up to 12 with the
  hero. A member who arrives with the 8 places full joins the bench, with everything they have.
- **You choose who fights.** In the camp menu's **Party Order**, L1 / R1 flips the right-hand
  column between the reserve and the bench, and you swap anyone but the hero in and out. Benched
  members keep their equipment, levels and skills, and you can manage them in the camp menu, but
  they aren't in play until you bring them in (Shattered Stars 0.02.51's release notes have the
  details).
- **`starting_character: any`** offers every member you haven't excluded.
- The healer guarantee is no longer needed: Rena and Noel are both in the pool unless you exclude
  them. More members also means more killer-move levels, crafts and learn levels as checks.
- It's the new option **`bench`**, **on by default**. Set `bench: false` for 0.2.0's 8 places.
  Story mode and open world without `character_items` keep the story's party and ignore it.
- **A seed with the bench needs Shattered Stars 0.02.51.** 0.02.50 refuses it ("unsupported
  version 4") instead of playing 12 members in 8 places.

## What's fixed

- **Open world with `expel_progression` off.** With the Expel teleporter on (the default), a
  Star Ocean world alone, or with only other Star Ocean players, could not be generated:
  Archipelago stopped with "No more spots to place ... Unplaced items: North City Pass". The
  North City Pass is the first pass Energy Nede's story needs, nothing there can be reached
  before it, and with `expel_progression` off it may not wait in Expel either. A multiworld
  with other games did generate, because their locations took the pass.
- **Open world with `boss_checks` off** and either `expel_progression` or `expel_teleporter` off
  failed the same way on the Noel's House Pass, whose only possible place was the Synard boss.
  This affected 0.2.0 with the teleporter off too.

**Now**, in open world, you start with the **North City Pass and the Noel's House Pass** as
well as the Arlia and Fun City passes, unless `expel_teleporter` and `expel_progression` are
both on (the defaults). Before, only the teleporter-off games had the North City Pass at the
start.

## What's new: Skillsanity checks can hold progression

With `skillsanity`, buying a set at a skill guild and reaching a level where a killer move or
spell used to be learned are checks. In 0.2.0 they only ever held filler and useful items.
Now they may hold progression items too (keys, characters, other worlds' progression), as long
as the logic can count on you reaching them:

- **Skill guild checks** are expected once one of the set's guilds is in reach: the sets up to
  1,600 Fol right away, the 2,700-4,500 Fol sets once you've finished Hilton and the Hoffmann
  Ruins (story mode: from the disc switch; hub mode: once Fienal opens). A guild you can lose
  for good, like old Clik's, never counts, and with `expel_progression` off only the guilds on
  Energy Nede do.
- **Learn levels** count as killer-move levels do: up to level 30 from the disc switch, higher
  ones from the Final Save Point (hub mode: from the start, higher ones once Fienal opens), and
  only for members the logic can count on. A member who joins through their character item needs
  it first, so that character becomes a progression item.
- Not with `encounter_rate: 0` (no battles, so no Fol and no levels), unless the seed is a hell
  seed (below). Precis's and Opera's machines, the Cave of Trials' learn chests and Float still
  hold no progression, and **shops still never do**.

This also fixes a rare mix that couldn't be generated at all: open world in Rena's story with
`expel_progression`, `boss_checks` and `enemy_dropsanity` off, moves and spells as items, and
killer-move checks for the hero. There were 60 move items needing a place, and only 63 places
that could take one.

## What's new: the hell seed

Set `encounter_rate: 0` (no random battles) together with `killer_move_checks`, or with
`skillsanity` `special_only` or `insanity` (learn levels), and you get a **hell seed**: a game
where the grind is meant to be preposterously hard. With no random battles, the only fights you
can train in are the **Fun City Fighting Arena**'s, so on a hell seed:

- **The arena is free.** Registering normally costs 2,000 Fol; a hell seed patches the fee to 0.
  Every arena fight still pays its EXP and Fol, and killer-move uses count there as anywhere.
  On every other seed the fee stays.
- **Killer-move levels, learn levels and skill guild checks count from the arena** and may hold
  progression items: in story mode from the disc switch, in open world once you've finished the
  Cave of Red Crystal (and hold the Fun City Pass, which you start with), in hub mode from the
  start. So a key you need may sit behind a long stretch of arena fights. That's the point.
- **Setup warns you.** Shattered Stars 0.02.51's setup shows "Hell Seed: no random battles.
  Killer-move levels and learn points are trained in the Fun City arena, which is free on this
  seed. Expect a very long grind." on its Archipelago page when you choose such a seed, and the
  game logs the same line. 0.02.50 plays a hell seed the same way, without the warning.

This also fixes the last mix known not to generate: the one above with `encounter_rate: 0`
added, where the moves those killer-move levels need were progression items with nowhere to go.

## Your seeds

- **Seeds made with 0.2.0 keep working** on Shattered Stars 0.02.50 and 0.02.51 as they are. A
  0.2.0 seed that generated is fine to play; there is no need to make it again.
- **An open-world player with `character_items`, or a hub player,** now gets the bench unless
  their YAML says `bench: false`: their pool, their checks and the seed change, and the seed needs
  Shattered Stars 0.02.51. With `bench: false` the same options and seed number make exactly the
  seed they made before the option.
- **With the default teleporter and `expel_progression`**, or in story mode or hub mode, and
  with `skillsanity` off (and the bench off, or not applying), 0.2.1 makes the same seed as 0.2.0
  from the same options and seed number: the same items in the same places. Only the version
  number written into the seed changes.
- **A player with either of those options off in open world** now starts with the two passes,
  so the same options and seed number place the multiworld's items otherwise.
- **A player with `skillsanity` on**, in any mode, may get guild checks and learn levels holding
  progression, so the same options and seed number place the multiworld's items otherwise.
- **A hell seed's player** (`encounter_rate: 0` with killer-move checks or learn levels) gets the
  free arena and the new rules above, so such a seed places its items otherwise too. Every other
  seed is unchanged by the hell seed.

## Installing

1. Copy `so2.apworld` into the `custom_worlds` folder of **Archipelago 0.6.8 or newer**,
   replacing the old one. Keep only one copy: Archipelago refuses to load the same game twice.
2. Generate as usual. Your options YAML from 0.2.0 works unchanged (the bench is then on, in
   open world with character items and in hub mode); the template,
   `Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml`, adds `bench` and describes the new starting passes, what
   Skillsanity's checks may now hold and the hell seed.
3. Play the seed on [Shattered Stars 0.02.51](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/v0.02.51) or later (0.02.50 plays a seed without the
   bench, and doesn't warn about a hell seed).

Details, every option, and troubleshooting: [Archipelago](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Archipelago)
on the wiki.

## What's in this release

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `so2.apworld` | The Archipelago world for Star Ocean: The Second Story, version 0.2.1. |
| `Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml` | The options template for that world. |
| `SHA256SUMS` | The SHA-256 sums of the two files (also below). |

The game itself is Shattered Stars, from [its own release](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/v0.02.51) (0.02.51 or later; 0.02.50
for seeds without the bench).

The world was checked with its own tests (699), Archipelago's general tests (379), 2,400 solo
fills of open-world games with `expel_progression` off, with and without the teleporter, the
boss checks and killer-move progression, 1,500 solo fills of Skillsanity mixes, 300 solo fills
of hell seeds, 500 solo fills of open-world and hub games with the bench, and batches of 96
seeds for each world mode, a batch of 96 solo games and a batch of 64 solo games without random
battles, all of which generated. With `bench: false`, the 288 batch seeds came out exactly as
before the option.

## Known limitations

See the [Shattered Stars 0.02.51 release notes](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/v0.02.51): the hub's few left-out scenes, the
port's Archipelago text in English on every release, and the rest.

## SHA-256 sums

```
83af433fa5f17a09e59b29eae859efd9df945e3b3eaefc59b04d6749f019849f  so2.apworld
93c41087a011bb2e8c54419c3a7ca1c44d96b2ccd1c8583a4fb277728eb7d035  Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml
```

apworld-v0.2.2.description:
# so2.apworld 0.2.2

Version 0.2.2 of the Archipelago world for *Star Ocean: The Second Story* adds **tracker
support**. [Universal Tracker](https://github.com/FarisTheAncient/Archipelago/releases) now
rebuilds your room exactly, without your YAML, and explains what a location needs. The room
carries its own logic, so the new PopTracker pack shows exactly what the world says. And in story
mode, with Shattered Stars 0.03.00 connected, both trackers follow the story. It makes the same
seeds as 0.2.1 from the same options and seed number, and plays on Shattered Stars 0.02.51 and
later.

It has its own release, apart from [the game's](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/v0.03.00)
and [the PopTracker pack's](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/poptracker-v1.0.0).
Get the game from [Shattered Stars 0.03.00](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/v0.03.00),
the pack from [PopTracker pack 1.0.0](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/poptracker-v1.0.0).

## What's new: Universal Tracker

Universal Tracker (UT) is an Archipelago client that lists the locations you can reach right now,
by the game's own logic, from what the server says you have received and checked. It builds this
world again on your machine and asks it. Until now that only worked by chance: UT made the world
again with another random seed and your YAML, and in open world with `character_items`, in hub
mode, or in story mode with `character_items`, the party it drew was not yours, so it showed the
wrong killer-move levels, crafts and learn levels (30 to 130 locations off in our tests).

Now:

- **No YAML needed.** UT rebuilds the world from the room's own data: every option, your party
  pool and, in hub mode, your start town. Install `tracker.apworld` and the room's `so2.apworld`
  in Archipelago's `custom_worlds` folder, open Universal Tracker from the Launcher and connect
  with your slot name. Your game can stay connected at the same time.
- **It is exact.** For every option mix we test (story, open world and hub mode, with and without
  the bench, every way the party can be drawn), the locations UT lists as reachable are exactly
  the ones the generator counted on, step by step through the whole game.
- **In story order.** UT's list runs through the areas in the order the story reaches them,
  Arlia first and the Cave of Trials last, then the skill guilds, learn levels, Item Creation and
  killer moves.
- **Excluded locations** (`exclude_locations`) show in UT's excluded group.
- **`/explain <location>` says what a location needs.** The world's rules are now data
  (Archipelago's Rule Builder) instead of code, so UT's `/explain` prints a location's rule, with
  what you have in green and what is missing in red, and the ways into its region. The logic is
  the same as 0.2.1's, rule for rule.
- **A room it can't track is refused, not tracked wrong.** Each room now says which logic it was
  made with (`logic_version`, 1). If the so2.apworld you installed can't rebuild the room (a room
  made with a newer version of this world, for example), UT says "The world has informed UT that
  your options are incompatible", and its `/faris_asked` command names the so2.apworld to install.
- **Universal Tracker's map tab.** UT now shows a map tab too: it carries its own map and
  location data (`apworld/so2/ut_map.py`, `apworld/so2/tracker/`) and takes its pictures from a
  zip, which UT asks you for once, by a file dialog, and remembers in `host.yaml`: either
  `so2_shattered_stars_ut.zip`, your own maps, which Shattered Stars 0.03.00 writes when it renders
  them from your disc (setup's **Render tracker maps for PopTracker**, or
  `--render-tracker-maps`), or the PopTracker pack's zip, with its plain stand-in maps. It follows
  the room the game reports and shows a marker for your party on the two world maps. When UT
  connects, the map tab opens on Expel's world map (with your marker if you are there) and follows
  your game from its next move: the next room, or a step on a world map. It has no doors: a door is not an AP location, entrance or event, so it carries no
  "which door leads where" of its own (that's PopTracker, below).

## What's new: logic for PopTracker

The room now carries the world's logic as data (the slot data's `tracker` key: its regions,
entrances, events and every location's rule, about 4 to 35 KB), so a tracker that can't run the
world itself can still show exactly what it says. The **PopTracker pack** (`so2_shattered_stars`
1.0.0, its own release) reads it: with a 0.2.2 room its map and board squares are green when a
check is in logic and red when not, the same as Universal Tracker, for every option and seed. The
format already has room for an entrance randomizer later: named entrances, and doors that stay
unconnected until found.

## What's new: story mode follows the story

Story mode's chapters need no items, so by the logic alone almost every check is reachable from the
start, and a tracker listed checks in towns the party hadn't reached yet. With Shattered Stars
0.03.00 connected to the room, the game tells the server which chapter it is in, and both trackers
now follow it:
- **Universal Tracker** lists only what the story has reached: a town's checks join the list when
  the story takes you there, Energy Nede's after the disc switch, the Cave of Trials and the
  chapter-60 scenes on Expel after the Final Save Point. It follows the chapter live, also back to an
  earlier save. `enforce_deferred_entrances: "off"` in host.yaml (UT's setting) turns it off.
- **The PopTracker pack** shows the checks later in the story in blue (and those the story has
  reached green, as before); its **Story** item turns that off, and its **Chapter** item can be set
  by hand when the game isn't connected.
- Before the game has connected, with an older Shattered Stars, and in open world and hub mode
  (whose stages are keyed) both show what the logic alone says, as before.

The story is followed by its 24 points: the start of each of the 23 story stages, and the Final
Save Point (chapter 60, step 4000). A stage is the unit: a gift first given in the middle of a stage
shows from the stage's start.

## Older rooms

- **Rooms made with 0.2.1** track in Universal Tracker with 0.2.2 installed, exactly: 0.2.1's
  logic is 0.2.2's.
- **Rooms made with 0.2.0** track with 0.2.2 too. With `skillsanity` on, UT warns in its log that
  0.2.1 changed the logic of Skillsanity's guild checks and learn levels (they may hold
  progression since, with stricter rules of their own): some of them may show up **later** than
  they really became reachable, never earlier. Measured on 45 such rooms (29 showed fewer at some
  point, 16 the same, none more) and on a player's own; regenerate with 0.2.2 for exact tracking.
- **A 0.2.0 hell seed** (`encounter_rate: 0` with killer-move checks) is refused: track it with
  so2.apworld 0.2.0 and your YAML in UT's Players folder.
- **In PopTracker**, rooms made with 0.2.0 or 0.2.1 have no logic in them: the pack shows every
  check as reachable (a checklist) and its banner says so. The pack's story awareness needs a
  0.2.2 room too.

## Your seeds

- **The seeds are the same.** 0.2.2 puts the same items in the same places as 0.2.1 from the same
  options and seed number, with the same spoilers (checked over the release workflow's 288 seeds).
  Only the version number written into the seed changes. The room's slot data gains three keys
  for trackers, `logic_version`, `exclude_locations` and `tracker` (in story mode with the story's
  points), which the game doesn't read.
- There are no new options: a YAML from 0.2.1 works as it is.
- Shattered Stars 0.02.51 plays every 0.2.2 seed; 0.02.50 every one without the bench, as with
  0.2.1. Shattered Stars 0.03.00 also tells your trackers your map and story.

## Installing

1. Copy `so2.apworld` into the `custom_worlds` folder of **Archipelago 0.6.8 or newer**,
   replacing the old one. Keep only one copy: Archipelago refuses to load the same game twice.
2. Generate as usual, with your options YAML or the template, `Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml`.
3. Play the seed on [Shattered Stars 0.03.00](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/v0.03.00)
   (0.02.51 plays it too, without the map and story for trackers).
4. Trackers: for Universal Tracker, put its `tracker.apworld` beside this `so2.apworld`; for
   PopTracker, get the [pack](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/poptracker-v1.0.0).
   How to set both up: [Trackers](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Trackers) on
   the wiki.

Details, every option, and troubleshooting: [Archipelago](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Archipelago)
on the wiki.

## What's in this release

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `so2.apworld` | The Archipelago world for Star Ocean: The Second Story, version 0.2.2. |
| `Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml` | The options template for that world. |
| `SHA256SUMS` | The SHA-256 sums of the two files (also below). |

The game itself is Shattered Stars, from [its own release](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/v0.03.00)
(0.03.00 for the tracker keys; 0.02.51 plays the seeds too).

The world was checked with its own tests (882, unchanged by the map tab), Archipelago's general
tests (379, and 935 scoped to this world), the slow tests' 700 rooms (320 rebuilt the way UT does
and compared at every sphere, 320 whose logic export was evaluated at every sphere, 60 story
rooms at 27 story positions each), the release workflow's 288 seeds, the same as 0.2.1's but the
version number (the map tab adds no slot-data key), and the real Universal Tracker 0.3.6 and
PopTracker 0.36.0 against local rooms: UT's list was the world's own in all 59 comparisons, the
story ones included; PopTracker's squares were too, at every point of its 45 checks (37 logic and
story checks, plus the room maps' door-click, door-colour and auto-tab step); and UT's own map tab loaded
16/16 of those rooms correctly, both from the repository world and from the packaged
`so2.apworld`, with the pack's zip and with the game's own zip of a render (every page's picture
through UT's own image loader).

## Known limitations

- **Story awareness follows stages, not single scenes.** A gift first given in the middle of a
  stage shows from the stage's start; Fienal's floors count from the last chapters' stage
  (chapter 58), though the party enters at chapter 60; the Final Save Point counts from the step
  before the save (chapter 60, step 4000).
- **PopTracker shows no "out of logic" (yellow).** The room's logic says what is in logic, not
  what could be done out of it.
- **Universal Tracker: don't turn Auto Tab off before UT connects.** With Auto Tab turned off
  (`/toggle_auto_tab`) before its first connect of a session, UT 0.3.6 drops the connection when it
  connects (an `AttributeError` about `location_icons` in its log; UT's own issue): connect first
  (once connected, the checkbox is fine), or turn it back on and `/connect` again.
- **Trackers update only while the game is online**: checks made offline show once the game
  reconnects and sends them.
- The rest: see the [Shattered Stars 0.03.00 release notes](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/releases/tag/v0.03.00).

## For developers

- `apworld/so2/ut.py`: the slot data -> option table, the checks, the refusal, the sort order,
  `LOGIC_VERSION` and when to bump it. docs/apworld/apworld.md "Trackers" and docs/apworld/seed_format.md
  "Slot data and trackers".
- `apworld/so2/logic.py`: the rules as Rule Builder data; `test/test_logic.py` keeps every rule a
  serialisable Rule Builder rule (docs/apworld/apworld.md "Rules as data").
- `test/test_ut.py` mirrors UT's rebuild and its fuzzer hook's sphere-by-sphere check without UT
  installed; `SO2_SLOW_TESTS=1` runs 20 seeds per mix. `trackers/tools/ap_ut_check.py` runs the real UT
  client headless against a local room (the release workflow).
- `apworld/so2/tracker_export.py` writes the `tracker` key (format 1: docs/apworld/seed_format.md "The
  tracker export"); `trackers/tools/ap_tracker_logic.py` is the reference evaluator, and `test/test_tracker.py`
  checks it against the world's own logic sphere by sphere and on random item states for every UT
  mix (`SO2_SLOW_TESTS=1`: 20 seeds each), plus the export's shape, round trip and size. The
  PopTracker pack's Lua evaluator is tested against the reference (trackers/tools/ap_poptracker_test.py) and
  in the real PopTracker 0.36.0 (trackers/tools/ap_poptracker_smoke.py).
- `apworld/so2/story.py`: story awareness, one source for both trackers: the story's points, each
  location's point, the export's `story` key, and Universal Tracker's deferred story events
  (`found_entrances_datastorage_key` = the port's `so2_story_{team}_{player}`,
  `reconnect_found_entrances`; only in UT's regeneration of a story-mode room, never with
  `enforce_deferred_entrances` off). docs/apworld/apworld.md "Story awareness", docs/apworld/seed_format.md
  "Story awareness". `test/test_story.py` checks UT's in-logic set against the reference
  evaluator's at every story point; trackers/tools/ap_ut_check.py and trackers/tools/ap_poptracker_smoke.py set the
  story key on a local server as the game does and check both real trackers follow it (UT: 142 of
  578 checks at chapter 3 up to all 578 at the Final Save Point; PopTracker: 37 green and 546 blue
  at chapter 3).

## SHA-256 sums

```
0212e0fd0c811cc8261ac3740d10694c98515d3dae7f2c05c6bb212ff175cdf7  so2.apworld
09b32d474b303daea70cddc3d86520f591182e5a063d4180a0f77f2c7cbb5c68  Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml
```

v0.01.00.description:
# Shattered Stars 0.01.00

The first release of Shattered Stars: a native Windows and Linux port of *Star Ocean: The
Second Story*, hand-written in C++20 on top of SDL3 and OpenGL. It is not an emulator — no
PlayStation code runs — and it ships no game data. You need your own disc images to play.

**You need your own North American discs:** SCUS-94421 (Disc 1) and SCUS-94422 (Disc 2), as a
`.cue` with its `.bin`, or an `.iso` / `.img`. European and Japanese discs, and compressed
formats such as CHD or PBP, aren't accepted yet. Disc 2 is optional until the story asks for
it.

## Highlights

- **Checked against the original, not by eye.** Every system was compared with the original
  game running in PCSX-Redux: frames, battle random-number draws, unit positions and damage,
  sound driver calls and save data.
- **Full speed, instant loading.** No slowdown when the screen gets busy, no waiting for the
  disc.
- **Bugs fixed, gameplay untouched.** 83 cases in the original's code are documented, each
  fixed only where the fix leaves hit timing, damage, difficulty and pacing exactly as they
  were, measured against the original.
- **Saves that travel.** Memory card images are byte-compatible with the console's; DexDrive
  saves convert in the setup program.
- **Modern controls and display.** Keyboard or gamepad, every button rebindable, analog
  walking and rumble; windowed, borderless or exclusive full screen, with optional
  PlayStation-style dithering and vertical sync.
- **Archipelago built in.** The multiworld client is part of the game itself — no separate
  client program.
- **Mods that never touch your discs.** Guarded patch files change chests, doors, items, shops
  and enemy stats as the game loads, managed from the setup program.
- **A setup program.** Choose and verify your disc images, and set display, sound, controls,
  memory cards, mods and Archipelago in one window.

## What's in this release

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ShatteredStars-0.01.00-win64.zip` | The Windows build: `shattered-stars.exe`, `setup.exe`, `SDL3.dll`, this project's `LICENSE`, `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt` and the README. |
| `ShatteredStars-0.01.00-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | The Linux build (needs glibc 2.36 or newer): `shattered-stars`, `shattered-stars-setup`, `LICENSE`, `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt` and the README. |
| `so2.apworld` | The Archipelago world for Star Ocean: The Second Story. |
| `Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml` | The options template for that world. |

There is no macOS build.

## Installing

1. Unpack the package for your platform anywhere.
2. Run the setup program: `setup.exe` on Windows, `./shattered-stars-setup` on Linux.
3. On the **Discs** page, choose Disc 1 and Disc 2 with **Browse...**, or put your images in
   the `discs` folder next to the game and press **Auto-detect**. Setup checks each image and
   says whether it is the right disc.
4. Press **Save & Play**.

After that, start the game directly with `shattered-stars.exe` or `./shattered-stars`.
Settings, memory cards and mods live in your user folder, so a later version can replace this
one without touching them.

Full details: [Installing and Setup](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Installing-and-Setup)
and [Playing](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Playing) on the wiki.

## Archipelago

Shattered Stars has the [Archipelago](https://archipelago.gg) client built into the game — no
separate client program is needed. This world is custom and **not yet part of Archipelago
itself**, so it ships here as a separate `.apworld`:

1. Copy `so2.apworld` into the `custom_worlds` folder of **Archipelago 0.6.8 or newer**.
2. Make your options YAML, either with the Archipelago Launcher's **Options Creator** (pick
   *Star Ocean: The Second Story* and set options with buttons and sliders) or by hand, starting
   from `Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml`.
3. Generate as usual. Each Star Ocean player gets a seed file ending in `.apso2`.
4. In the setup program's **Archipelago** page, choose the seed file and enter the room's
   address, your slot name and password. Press **Save & Play**; the game connects as it
   starts.

Details, every option, and troubleshooting: [Archipelago](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Archipelago)
on the wiki.

## Known limitations

- **North American discs only.** SCUS-94421 / SCUS-94422. European and Japanese releases, and
  compressed disc formats (CHD, PBP), are not accepted yet.
- **No macOS build.**
- **The Archipelago world is not yet in Archipelago itself.** Until it's merged upstream, get
  `so2.apworld` and its template from this project's releases, not the Archipelago Launcher's
  own world list.
- **The curated mod list is small.** Two sample mods ship today; see the
  [Modding](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Modding) wiki page to make or
  submit your own.

See [Bugs Fixed and Quirks Kept](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Bugs-Fixed-and-Quirks-Kept)

v0.02.00.description:
# Shattered Stars 0.02.00

Shattered Stars now plays the European (English), French and German releases of *Star Ocean:
The Second Story* as well as the North American one, in the same build: the game recognises
your discs and plays their release. This release also ships version 0.1.1 of the Archipelago
world, which fixes open-world seeds.

Shattered Stars is a native Windows and Linux port, hand-written in C++20 on top of SDL3 and
OpenGL. It is not an emulator — no PlayStation code runs — and it ships no game data. You need
your own disc images to play.

**You need your own discs from one of these releases**, as a `.cue` with its `.bin`, or an
`.iso` / `.img`. Both discs must come from the same release. Disc 2 is optional until the story
asks for it.

| Release | Disc 1 | Disc 2 | Text | Save product code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| North American | SCUS-94421 | SCUS-94422 | English | BASCUS-94421 |
| European | SCES-02159 | SCES-12159 | English | BASCES-02159 |
| French | SCES-02160 | SCES-12160 | French | BESCES-02160 |
| German | SCES-02161 | SCES-12161 | German | BESCES-02161 |

Japanese discs (SLPM-86105 / SLPM-86106) are recognised but not supported yet.

## What's new

- **The European, French and German releases.** Each plays with its own text and data — its
  translation, fonts, menus, name entry and credits — on the North American game logic at
  60 Hz: the same gameplay that was checked against the original, at the full frame rate. On
  both discs, the European release runs every event entry of the field maps with the same
  results as the North American one. The French and German releases do too, except where the
  automated test answered a choice differently because their longer option text shifts its
  timing. All 564 battles of the game play out identically, frame for frame, in all three.
- **French and German text, checked against the originals.** Word wrap, accented letters, the
  name-entry keyboards, the camp menu, the Options pages and the rename page work as in the
  French and German originals running in PCSX-Redux. Every line of the opening laid out by the
  port matches the original's (88 of 88 in French, 84 of 84 in German), and so do the French
  battle result screen and the German Scan window.
- **Saves in each release's own format.** A save carries its release's product code, save
  signature and icon setting, so a card works with that release's console and emulators. In
  PCSX-Redux, the North American, European, French and German originals each list and load a
  save the port wrote, and the port loads a save the French original wrote.
- **Setup knows the releases.** The Discs page names each disc's release ("Disc 1, French
  release: OK"), and refuses a pair from two releases: "Disc 2 is the European release and
  Disc 1 the French one. Both discs must be the same release." A Japanese disc gets a clear
  message naming the releases Shattered Stars plays.
- **Archipelago world 0.1.1.** It fixes open-world logic errors that could make a seed
  impossible to finish, and the ship to El now waits until you hold the El passes (see
  [Archipelago](#archipelago)). One seed now works with the discs of any supported release.
- **Mods on every release.** Mod lines name places as they are on the North American disc, and
  the game translates them for the disc you play; a line whose data differs in that release is
  skipped, as before. `tools/so2_mod.py` reads the North American, European, French or German
  disc. Both sample mods pass the maintainer's verification on the European disc.

The work on the other releases leaves the North American discs as they were: every test suite,
the quick reference set and the smoke test pass on them unchanged, and their saves are written
byte for byte as before.

## What's in this release

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ShatteredStars-0.02.00-win64.zip` | The Windows build: `shattered-stars.exe`, `setup.exe`, `SDL3.dll`, this project's `LICENSE`, `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt` and the README. |
| `ShatteredStars-0.02.00-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | The Linux build (needs glibc 2.36 or newer): `shattered-stars`, `shattered-stars-setup`, `LICENSE`, `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt` and the README. |
| `so2.apworld` | The Archipelago world for Star Ocean: The Second Story, version 0.1.1. |
| `Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml` | The options template for that world. |

There is no macOS build.

## Installing

1. Unpack the package for your platform anywhere.
2. Run the setup program: `setup.exe` on Windows, `./shattered-stars-setup` on Linux.
3. On the **Discs** page, choose Disc 1 and Disc 2 with **Browse...**, or put your images in
   the `discs` folder next to the game and press **Auto-detect**. Setup checks each image and
   says which disc and release it is.
4. Press **Save & Play**.

After that, start the game directly with `shattered-stars.exe` or `./shattered-stars`.

**Updating from 0.01.00:** unpack the new package and use it in place of the old one.
Settings, memory cards and mods live in your user folder, so they stay as they are. If you
keep your disc images in the old package's `discs` folder, move them across.

Full details: [Installing and Setup](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Installing-and-Setup)
and [Playing](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Playing) on the wiki.

## Archipelago

> **Open-world players: generate your seed again with `so2.apworld` 0.1.1.** In 0.1.0, about
> 4 in 10 seeds with `world_mode: open_world` could not be finished at all, and in almost every
> one a key could be left behind for good when the ship sails to El. Story mode, the default,
> was never affected: 0.1.1 generates story-mode seeds exactly as 0.1.0 did. A seed made with
> 0.1.0 still loads, but without the new gates below.

What 0.1.1 fixes, in open world only (the item pool, location names and ids are unchanged):

- **Two ship landings were missing from the logic.** The Lacour continent is reached only by
  the Herlie ship, which lands at Port Hilton, and Hoffmann Ruins only by the Hilton ship, which
  lands on its beach. 0.1.0 could put the Hilton Pass in Lacour Castle, or the Map 231 Pass in
  Hoffmann Ruins: places you can't reach without those very keys. 0.1.1 requires the landing's
  key for every area reached by ship.
- **The teleporter doesn't reach Expel's islands.** The old man in Fun City's arena takes you
  back to Expel, but only to the continents you can walk to or reach by the Herlie ferry.
  Hoffmann Ruins and Eluria Colony, which only the story's ships reach, could hold another
  player's progression or a key the story needs after the disc change, lost for good if you
  hadn't picked it up first. In 0.1.1 they hold only the Expel story's own keys, which you
  collect before Expel closes.
- **The ship to El waits for the El passes.** After the battle at the Lacour Front Line, the
  meeting at the Front Line starts a chain of scenes that ends at sea: once you are on
  El, the Cross and Lacour continents and Hoffmann Ruins stay out of reach until much later.
  0.1.0 could leave the El Beach, Eluria or Eluria Tower Pass back there. Now the logic puts
  those passes where you can still get them before you sail, and the game doesn't start that
  meeting until you hold all three: walking into it shows "El Beach Pass needed to sail"
  for each one you're missing, and you can go and fetch them first.
- **The teleporter needs the Synard.** Fun City lies on a different island of Energy Nede
  from Central City, so you can only reach the arena's teleporter once the Synard flies. 0.1.0
  counted on it from your first walk on Energy Nede. With the Expel Teleporter and Expel
  Progression options both on — the defaults in open world — other players' progression can
  sit in Expel until the Synard, so the ship to El now also waits for the North City, Noel's
  House and Red Crystal Passes, which the story needs before then.
- **No walking out of Central City or Noel's House too early.** The story brings you into
  both without going through their entrance. Until the story is done there (chapters 38 and 40),
  their exit asks for that area's pass ("Central City Pass needed to leave"), so you can't
  lock yourself out on an island you can't leave yet.

The fix was proven with the world's tests, Archipelago's general tests, a 96-seed batch with
no error (the 0.1.0 batch had an unreachable key in 44 of its 114 open-world slots, and an El
pass you could sail away from in 110), the late-game, teleporter and voyage proofs, and
end-to-end games against a local server.

Shattered Stars has the [Archipelago](https://archipelago.gg) client built into the game — no
separate client program is needed. This world is custom and **not yet part of Archipelago
itself**, so it ships here as a separate `.apworld`:

1. Copy `so2.apworld` into the `custom_worlds` folder of **Archipelago 0.6.8 or newer**,
   replacing 0.1.0. Keep only one copy: Archipelago refuses to load the same game twice.
2. Make your options YAML, either with the Archipelago Launcher's **Options Creator** (pick
   *Star Ocean: The Second Story* and set options with buttons and sliders) or by hand, starting
   from `Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml`.
3. Generate as usual. Each Star Ocean player gets a seed file ending in `.apso2`.
4. In the setup program's **Archipelago** page, choose the seed file and enter the room's
   address, your slot name and password. Press **Save & Play**; the game connects as it
   starts.

A seed works with North American, European, French and German discs alike, so the players of
one multiworld can each use their own release. The full end-to-end test against a local
server passed on the European and the French discs.

Details, every option, and troubleshooting: [Archipelago](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Archipelago)
on the wiki.

## Known limitations

- **Japanese discs aren't supported yet.** Setup recognises them and says so. The Japanese
  release is a different build of the game, with its own changes to enemies, party moves,
  spells and text; it is planned for a later release.
- **The PAL versions' 50 Hz timing isn't reproduced, by design.** European, French and German
  discs play on the North American game logic at 60 Hz. The PAL versions scaled movement and
  the camera by 6/5 per frame to make up for their slower frame rate, and removed the clash of
  opposing elemental projectiles (which cancel or overpower each other); neither change is
  used, so the projectile clash stays on as in the North American game. The PAL versions also
  added the item spells The Scream and Judgement Day to the spells that never clash with
  another caster's; the port keeps the North American list, so on PAL discs those two can still
  clash. The credits' timing,
  which the PAL data counts in 50 Hz frames, is converted to 60 Hz. Each release keeps its own
  text, credits and rumble lengths.
- **Saves stay with their release.** The game uses the saves of the release you play.
  Importing a save from another release isn't offered yet.
- **Compressed disc formats** (CHD, PBP) are not accepted yet.
- **No macOS build.**
- **The Archipelago world is not yet in Archipelago itself.** Until it's merged upstream, get
  `so2.apworld` and its template from this project's releases, not the Archipelago Launcher's
  own world list.
- **French and German Archipelago messages** use the game's own font: a symbol it doesn't have
  in a player or item name shows as a similar character, or a space.
- **Open world: the ship to El won't sail without its keys.** The voyage to El is still one
  way until the disc change, so a key left elsewhere on Expel couldn't be fetched after it:
  0.1.0 could do this to you. 0.1.1 fixes it instead of just warning about it: the El Beach,
  Eluria and Eluria Tower Passes stay reachable before you sail, and with the Expel Teleporter
  and Expel Progression options both on (the open-world defaults) so do the North City, Noel's
  House and Red Crystal Passes. The game won't start the voyage until you hold all of the ones
  that apply, and names whichever you're still missing (see [Archipelago](#archipelago) above).
- **The curated mod list is small.** Two sample mods ship today; see the
  [Modding](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Modding) wiki page to make or
  submit your own.

See [Bugs Fixed and Quirks Kept](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Bugs-Fixed-and-Quirks-Kept)
for what was changed from the original and what was deliberately left as it was.

## Licence and legal

Shattered Stars' own code is released under the [MIT licence](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/blob/main/LICENSE). Third-party
components keep their own licences, listed in each package's `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt`.

This release contains none of *Star Ocean: The Second Story*'s program files or data. To play,
you need your own, legally obtained copy of the game's discs; nothing can be downloaded here.
This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Square Enix, tri-Ace or Sony Interactive
Entertainment.

a147ae203ae9cfcae99f8caf54181bc9b8efe170d84ed81da3a30be8e557f762  ShatteredStars-0.02.00-win64.zip
29afa139dd7c1c501e830e70c9bf9c22dfd38e24b400d1cbf11b5886403cf7ad  so2.apworld

v0.02.50.description:
# Shattered Stars 0.02.50

This release ships version 0.2.0 of the Archipelago world, its first major revision: a new
**hub mode** that opens the whole game at once, item creation, killer moves, skills and spells
as checks, three goals, three difficulty settings, a character select and a reworked open-world
party. The port gains the setup side to go with it: seeds straight from Archipelago's archive,
a memory card for each seed, an on / off switch, and settings for instant text and
auto-advance. It also fixes saving on Windows for players whose folders have accented names,
and such names on a command line, a weapon graphic, a soft-lock in open-world seeds and several
smaller faults.

Shattered Stars is a native Windows and Linux port, hand-written in C++20 on top of SDL3 and
OpenGL. It is not an emulator — no PlayStation code runs — and it ships no game data. You need
your own disc images to play.

**You need your own discs from one of these releases**, as a `.cue` with its `.bin`, or an
`.iso` / `.img`. Both discs must come from the same release. Disc 2 is optional until the story
asks for it (Archipelago's hub mode asks for it at New Game).

| Release | Disc 1 | Disc 2 | Text |
|---|---|---|---|
| North American | SCUS-94421 | SCUS-94422 | English |
| European | SCES-02159 | SCES-12159 | English |
| French | SCES-02160 | SCES-12160 | French |
| German | SCES-02161 | SCES-12161 | German |

Japanese discs (SLPM-86105 / SLPM-86106) are recognised but not supported yet.

## What's new

- **Archipelago world 0.2.0**, with a hub mode, craftsanity, killer-move checks, skillsanity,
  goals, difficulty and the open-world party (see [Archipelago world 0.2.0](#archipelago-world-020)).
  **Seeds made with it need Shattered Stars 0.02.50.**
- **Seeds straight from the archive.** Setup's **Archipelago** page takes the `AP_<number>.zip`
  that Archipelago writes, as it is: there is no need to unpack it. **Browse...** starts in
  Archipelago's own `output` folder. When the archive holds more than one Star Ocean player, a
  **Your slot** list lets you pick yours.
- **A memory card for each seed.** A seed now saves on a card of its own, kept in an
  `archipelago` folder beside your settings, never on your ordinary cards. Your own saves can't
  be loaded into a seed, and a seed can't overwrite them. The Archipelago page shows how many
  saves the seed has, with **Open folder** to find them.
- **Archipelago on or off.** A switch on the **Archipelago** row of setup's sidebar turns it off:
  you play the original game on your own cards, and the seed and server stay filled in for
  next time.
- **Saves that stay with their seed.** With a seed, only that seed's own saves load. A save
  from another seed, an ordinary save, or a save changed outside the game is refused with the
  game's own "The data could not be loaded" message. This guards against accidents and casual
  save editing; it is not meant as cheat protection.
- **No debugging in an Archipelago game.** A game played with a seed ignores the debugging
  options (the debug console, map and battle starts, and the like), and its log says which ones
  it ignored.
- **Dialogue at your pace.** Setup has a new **Gameplay** page with **Instant text** (each
  message page appears at once) and **Auto-advance** (pages move on by themselves after a wait
  of 0.5 to 3 seconds, but never past a choice; the battle result screen too). Both are off by
  default and work in every game, with or without Archipelago. The game itself plays exactly as
  before.
- **The story route skips its screens.** When a seed was made for Claude's or Rena's story,
  New Game skips the hero select and the naming screen and starts that hero's game, with the
  default name.
- **An icon and a name of its own.** Both programs show an icon (an original design) and their
  names, "Shattered Stars" and "Shattered Stars Setup", in the title bar, the taskbar and Task
  Manager (which called the game "POSIX WinThreads for Windows" before). On Linux,
  `install-desktop-entry.sh` adds both to the application menu, so the taskbar shows them on
  GNOME and KDE Wayland too.
- **Esc asks before quitting.** Esc no longer closes the game at once: it pauses the game and
  asks "Quit Shattered Stars?", with **Keep playing** highlighted. Left / Right choose, Enter
  (or Cross on the gamepad, as you have it bound) picks, and Esc again goes back to the game,
  exactly where it was. The window's close button and Alt+F4 still close it straight away.
- **Fixes**, among them saving on Windows, Claude's sword in Rena's game and a soft-lock in
  open-world seeds (see [Fixes](#fixes)).

## Archipelago world 0.2.0

### Hub mode

`world_mode: hub` is a new way to play. New Game starts at the end of the story's journey, after
the Final Save Point on disc 2, with both worlds open, the Synard parked beside you, and every
location still to find. From there the game is yours to take in any order:

- **Dungeons open with their keys.** Each dungeon has a key ("Salva Drift Key", "Cave of Red
  Crystal Key", ...), found in the multiworld; a locked entrance names the key it needs. A
  dungeon with nothing behind it needs no key. The towns, their shops and their chests are open
  from the start.
- **Every story boss waits in its chamber.** 22 bosses, from Alen-Tax to Berle, play their
  original scene and fight where the story put them, and each win is a check. Three of them
  wait in towns: Berle in Armlock, Shigeo in Fun City and Marsilio in the arena.
- **Shigeo and Marsilio ask first.** Shigeo's street is on the way from Energy Nede back to
  Expel, so walking into it asks "Face Shigeo now?". Say no and you walk on through; he asks
  again on your next visit, once you've been back on the world map. The arena's desk offers
  "Face Marsilio." beside "Register.", so the ordinary arena stays open for training.
- **Fienal opens on the bosses.** Its gate needs no key: it opens once you've beaten the bosses
  `fienal_requirement` names, and shows which ones are left ("Defeat Magichand first").
  Indalecio waits inside.
- **The story stays where it is.** Scenes that would move the story on are held back, and
  nothing closes behind you: no disc change, no one-way voyage.
- **Start where you like.** `hub_start` picks Fun City (the default), Arlia, or a random one of
  16 towns on either world. Crossing between the worlds needs no key: the arena's old man in Fun
  City and the guide in Arlia take you across.
- **Characters are items** in hub mode; nobody joins through the story.

Each of the 22 boss chambers was played through in both heroes' games, all 16 starts were tested
in both, a search of the whole hub game confirmed what each seed can reach, and a 96-seed batch
and an end-to-end game against a local server passed.

### New options

| Option | Values (default first) | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `world_mode` | `story`, `open_world`, **`hub`** | Hub mode is new (above). |
| `hub_start` | `fun_city`, `arlia`, `random_town` | Where a hub game starts. |
| `fienal_requirement` | `fields_and_berle`, `fields`, `all_bosses` | What opens Fienal in a hub game: the four Fields' bosses and Berle, the Fields only, or every story boss outside Fienal. |
| `goal` | `indalecio`, `indalecio_limiter_off`, `indalecio_limiter_off_and_iseria_queen` | Beat Indalecio as before (`final_boss` still works), or his stronger form after Filia removes the limiter in Central City, or that and the Iseria Queen too. The way to Indalecio stays shut, with a message, until the goal's conditions are met. |
| `difficulty` | `earth`, `galaxy`, `universe`, `any` | The Battle Rank. New Game sets it and skips the screen; `any` shows the screen with all three offered. Only the monsters' strength changes, so the logic is the same. |
| `craftsanity` | off, on | The first time you make each item with Item Creation is a check: 553 of them, Publishing's books included. You keep what you made. |
| `no_fail_crafting` | off, on | Item Creation never fails by chance. |
| `killer_move_checks` | off, on | Each proficiency level of a killer move is a check: 133 of them. |
| `killer_move_progression` | `never`, `hero`, `any` | Whether those checks may hold progression: never, only the hero's moves, or any member's. |
| `skillsanity` | `none`, `skills_only`, `special_only`, `insanity` | Skills, or killer moves and spells, or both, become items. Buying a guild's skill set gives a check for each skill in it, and each point where a member would learn a move or spell is a check (148). With moves and spells as items, a member starts with only their first move and learns the rest as they arrive. |
| `skillsanity_shop_share` | 10 (0-100) | With skillsanity and shop shuffling, the share of skill and move items sold in shops as themselves. |
| `drop_progression` | `allow`, `force`, `never` | With `enemy_dropsanity`, whether an enemy's first drop may hold progression. Only enemies you can always meet again, and only drops with fair odds, ever do. |
| `area_keys_in_drops` | on, off | Whether open-world area keys may be in drops. |
| `starting_character` | `hero`, `any`, or a name | Open world and hub: who joins at the start and leads the party. `any` lets you pick at New Game, on a new character select. |
| `exclude_characters` | none | Open world and hub: members who never join. |

**Renamed options.** `protagonist` is now `story_route`, and `drops_as_checks` is now
`enemy_dropsanity`. **Rename them in your old YAML files**: Archipelago ignores the old names,
with a warning, and uses the defaults instead (`any` and `off`).

### What else changed

- **The open-world party** (open world with `character_items`): no member locks out another any
  more, Leon and Dias join in either hero's game, the other hero and Noel can be items too, and
  if your party could end up with no healer, the world makes sure Rena or Noel is in it. The
  story's own party splits still happen, and members set aside come back when they're over.
- **Your leader walks the field.** In open world and hub mode, the Formation leader you choose
  in the camp menu (your starting character, from the start) is the one you see on field maps,
  and the story's lines call them by name, in the hub's boss scenes too. The hero comes back on
  the world map and for the scenes that need them. This is only how it looks: the story plays
  as it would.
- **New members join at the party's level.** In open world and hub mode, a member who joins
  starts at the middle level of the party, not the level the story would give them.
- **Port Hilton's captain** (open world): the sailor offers the voyages open to you right now —
  Cross, Hoffmann Ruins, El (when the story is ready to sail and you hold its passes), or "Not
  now". Ships check their landing's key before taking your fare.
- **Shop slots give what you buy.** With `shuffle_shops`, the first purchase of a slot now gives
  you everything you bought and the slot's check as well. A slot still to check has the
  Archipelago logo after its name. This works for existing seeds too.
- **Gift sites never hold progression**, in any world mode.
- **The Cave of Trials by its real floors.** Its locations were all named "Cave of Trials Level
  1: ..."; they now carry their real floor ("Cave of Trials Level 7: ..."), and the treasure
  vault and the Weird Beast's arena have their own names. Three boss names were corrected the
  same way (Phoenix is on floor 12, G-Celesta on 13, Weirdbeast in its arena). The location ids
  are unchanged.
- **Three Cave of Trials chests are gone.** "Portrait F / G / J chest" in 0.1.x were not chests
  but the spots that teach Leon Extinction, Ashton tri-Ace and Celine Meteor Swarm. They are
  no longer locations (with skillsanity they come back as learn points), so a seed with
  `cave_of_trials` has three locations fewer.

The world was proven with its own tests (380), Archipelago's general tests (379), batches of 96
seeds for each world mode with no error, the late-game and hub proofs, and end-to-end games
against a local server, both in story and open world and in hub mode.

## Fixes

- **Saving on Windows.** When the folder holding the memory card had a name with letters
  outside plain English — a Windows user name such as "José" or "Jürgen", or an Archipelago
  slot name like "Cléo" — saving seemed to work but wrote nothing, and the save was gone the
  next time the game started. Saves now land wherever the card lives. Linux was not affected.
- **Accented names on the Windows command line.** Starting the game or setup from a command
  line or a shortcut with such a path, for example `--memcard1 "C:\Games\Test Ä\card.mcd"`,
  stopped both at once ("Cannot convert character sequence"). Every path on the command line
  and in the `SS_` variables now works whatever its letters, and the console shows them as
  written. Playing through setup was never affected.
- **The log keeps the Archipelago lines.** `shattered-stars.log`, beside `config.ini` (the file
  to attach to a bug report), now holds every line the console shows: the seed, checks, items,
  saves and loads, and the server's messages. It stays under 4 MB however long you play.
- **Archipelago servers** now see the game as a client of Archipelago 0.6.8, the version this
  world needs, instead of 0.6.6.
- **Setup's Auto-detect**, with Disc 1 already chosen, found Disc 2 but said "Found Disc 2, but
  no Disc 1." It now says it found Disc 2 next to your Disc 1.
- **A debug line**, the original game's "pwnd->destroy", no longer appears each time a menu
  window closes.
- **Claude's sword in Rena's game.** A party member who fights with a weapon drew the wrong,
  stretched weapon picture whenever they weren't first in the party: Claude in Rena's game, for
  one, from the Alen-Tax fight on. Every weapon user now draws their own weapon, wherever they
  stand.
- **Open world: stuck on the Lacour continent.** In chapters 23 and 24, Port Hilton's sailor —
  the only way off the continent — refused to sail, while the seed could have put the keys you
  needed next on Cross. He now takes you. This affected open-world seeds from so2.apworld 0.1.0
  and 0.1.1; the new port alone repairs them, with no new seed needed.
- **Archipelago shops.** Buying a shop slot gave the check instead of what you bought; it now
  gives both (above). A slot whose check was Fol lost that Fol when the purchase was paid; it now
  arrives. The mark for a slot still to check never showed in 0.02.00; it does now.
- **The Cave of Trials' learn chests in 0.1.x seeds** read and wrote past the party's records.
  Now nothing is changed: opening one gives or sends the item its location holds.
- **Courier orders in Archipelago games.** An order that would take an item past 20 was lost
  entirely, a fault of the original game. With a seed, the copies that fit are delivered and the
  rest wait for you as received items. Without a seed, the original's behaviour is kept.
- **Two story scenes** — the Field of Courage before its Guardian, and Eluria Tower before Berle
  — left the script engine one value out of step after the next battle, a fault of the original
  game that could crash the port later. Fixed; nothing you see or hear changes.
- **Menus** read past the end of their window graphics each time they opened. Nothing visible
  changes, but a possible crash is gone.
- **The debug console** (`--debug`) could leave the game hanging as it quit, when started from
  a terminal or a pipe. It now quits at once, on Linux and Windows. Its status line now reaches
  the window title under X11 too ("Shattered Stars - map 18 | ...").

## Updating from 0.02.00

Unpack the new package and use it in place of the old one. Settings, memory cards and mods live
in your user folder, so they stay as they are. If you keep your disc images in the old
package's `discs` folder, move them across.

**Seeds and runs in progress:**

| Seed made with | On Shattered Stars 0.02.00 | On Shattered Stars 0.02.50 |
|---|---|---|
| so2.apworld 0.1.0 / 0.1.1 | plays | plays, with this release's fixes |
| so2.apworld 0.2.0 | refused ("unsupported version"), or plays without some of its settings | plays |

- **You don't need to generate your seed again.** A 0.1.1 seed keeps working and gains the fixes
  above: the Lacour soft-lock, the shop purchases, the Cave of Trials chests. Generate with 0.2.0
  only for the new options. (Open-world seeds from 0.1.0 still have that version's logic errors:
  0.02.00's advice to regenerate them with 0.1.1 or newer stands.)
- **A run in progress carries on.** The first time 0.02.50 starts a seed, it copies that seed's
  saves from your memory card onto the seed's own card, once. Your own card is left as it is.
- **0.2.0 seeds need the new port.** Shattered Stars 0.02.50 reads every seed so2.apworld 0.1.0,
  0.1.1 and 0.2.0 make. Everyone playing Star Ocean in a 0.2.0 multiworld needs 0.02.50.
- **What a 0.1.x seed plays differently on 0.02.50:** a seed made for one hero's story skips the
  hero select instead of holding the cursor; in open world, new members join at the party's
  level, and your Formation leader walks the field; and the fixes above.

## Installing

1. Unpack the package for your platform anywhere.
2. Run the setup program: `setup.exe` on Windows, `./shattered-stars-setup` on Linux.
3. On the **Discs** page, choose Disc 1 and Disc 2 with **Browse...**, or put your images in
   the `discs` folder next to the game and press **Auto-detect**. Setup checks each image and
   says which disc and release it is.
4. Press **Save & Play**.

After that, start the game directly with `shattered-stars.exe` or `./shattered-stars`.

Full details: [Installing and Setup](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Installing-and-Setup)
and [Playing](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Playing) on the wiki.

## Playing with Archipelago

Shattered Stars has the [Archipelago](https://archipelago.gg) client built into the game — no
separate client program is needed. This world is custom and **not yet part of Archipelago
itself**, so it ships here as a separate `.apworld`:

1. Copy `so2.apworld` into the `custom_worlds` folder of **Archipelago 0.6.8 or newer**,
   replacing the old one. Keep only one copy: Archipelago refuses to load the same game twice.
2. Make your options YAML, either with the Archipelago Launcher's **Options Creator** or by
   hand, starting from `Star.Ocean.The.Second.Story.yaml`.
3. Generate as usual. Archipelago writes `AP_<number>.zip` into its `output` folder.
4. In the setup program's **Archipelago** page, press **Browse...** and choose that archive (or
   a loose `.apso2` seed file), pick your slot if it asks, and enter the room's address, your
   slot name and the password. Press **Save & Play**; the game connects as it starts.

To play a seed on your own, leave the address empty. A seed works with the discs of any
supported release, so the players of one multiworld can each use their own.

Details, every option, and troubleshooting: [Archipelago](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Archipelago)
on the wiki.

## Known limitations

- **Old option names.** YAML files written for 0.1.x that use `protagonist` or
  `drops_as_checks` need those keys renamed (see [New options](#new-options)).
- **Hub mode leaves a few things out:** the story's scenes outside the boss chambers, the early gifts,
  the Lacour tournament, the fights the story lets you lose, the Portal of Sealing, the
  Nightmare, Flarelizard and Ghost fights, and the arena's prize. Scenes where the story splits
  the party are fought with the whole party.
- **The text the port adds for Archipelago is in English** on every release: the messages, the
  hub's questions, Port Hilton's captain, and the short descriptions on the character select.
  French and German Archipelago messages use the game's own font, so a symbol it lacks in a
  player or item name shows as a similar character, or a space. In French and German shops, a
  very long item name may run under the Archipelago logo.
- **Excluding both Rena and Noel** with `exclude_characters` can leave an open-world party with no
  healer.
- **Your leader on the field** gives way to the hero in a few places: a dash's afterimages show
  the hero, and so does a long scene until free play returns.
- **Port Hilton's captain:** taking his Hoffmann Ruins voyage in chapter 23 skips the soldier's
  lines of that first trip.
- **With skillsanity**, the Cave of Trials' learn spots still say the move was learned; the move
  itself arrives as its item.
- **Instant text and auto-advance** are set in setup only, not from inside the game.
- **Japanese discs aren't supported yet.** Setup recognises them and says so.
- **The PAL versions' 50 Hz timing isn't reproduced, by design.** European, French and German
  discs play on the North American game logic at 60 Hz, with their own text.
- **Saves stay with their release.** Importing a save from another release isn't offered yet.
- **Compressed disc formats** (CHD, PBP) are not accepted yet.
- **No macOS build.**
- **The Archipelago world is not yet in Archipelago itself.** Until it's merged upstream, get
  `so2.apworld` and its template from this project's releases.

See [Bugs Fixed and Quirks Kept](https://github.com/IronJade/Shattered-Stars/wiki/Bugs-Fixed-and-Quirks-Kept)
for what was changed from the original and what was deliberately left as it was.
